lines.text: Did you know that American dollar bills are not actually made out of paper?
If they were made of wood pulp paper, a single accidental trip through the laundry washing machine would turn them into mush.
U.S. currency is printed on a unique blend of seventy-five percent cotton and twenty-five percent linen.
Tiny red and blue synthetic fibers are woven directly into the fabric to defeat counterfeiters.
Giant intaglio printing presses stamp sheets under twenty tons of pressure, creating raised ink textures you can feel with your fingernail.
Color-shifting bells and 3D security ribbons turn bills into high-tech security sheets.
A dollar bill can be folded over four thousand times before it finally tears.
